Second SFI (Grade R, Term 4, same Skill Area and Sub-strand): 'Copies print from the environment when playing such as labels from advertisements'. Both are emergent-writing copying-from-environmental-print skills and are substantively coherent and complementary: pretend writing with copied letters/numerals and copying printed labels during play reinforce the same emerging understanding of print as reproducible meaning. However, developmental extension is not established: the second endpoint's Learning Component (b265347d) carries a second claim with the Grade R / TERM 3 ancestor path (TERM 3 f5f4d44a, Skill Area e974dc46, Sub-strand bad5cd4b) from SFI e1aebc9f with the same copies-print-when-playing wording, and the first endpoint's merge_reason enumerates a separate Term 3 'copying environmental print' bullet. The Term 4 capability therefore already exists in Term 3, making this CAPS within-grade recurrence rather than expanded capability, so buildsTowards is not supported in either direction; the coherence is more than generic repetition, so canonical symmetric relatesTo applies with endpoint order unchanged and null direction. Shared Grade ancestor, Sub-strand wording and LC token overlap were not treated as evidence on their own. All endpoint/ancestor audit-merge warnings and the source-evidence truncation (24 omitted items per endpoint) are retained and limit, but do not contradict, this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade R (rank 0) Skills in the same Skill Area (LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL)) and the same printed sub-strand ('Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects'), differing in Term: Term 1 'Listens to short stories with enjoyment and joins in choruses at the appropriate time' (LCs: 'Listens to short stories with enjoyment'; 'Joins in choruses at the appropriate time') and Term 3 'Listens to announcements and responds appropriately' (LCs: 'Listens to announcements'; 'Responds appropriately to announcements'). The two statements are coherent and mutually reinforcing: each pairs attentive listening with a contextually appropriate response in Grade R oral work, so classroom work on one meaningfully supports and complements the other. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Term 4, Skill Area 'EMERGENT WRITING' (rank 0, same term), but under different sub-strands: 'Emergent Writing:' for the directionality statement and 'Works with words' for the shared/dictated class writing. The first concerns print-concept conventions ('writes' left to right, top to bottom of page); the second concerns oral composition of sentences that the teacher scribes. These are complementary facets of emergent writing (handling of print vs. generating connected text) that reinforce one another, but neither statement's evidence shows that proficiency in one materially supports success in the other, and both are in the same term so no earlier-to-later developmental ordering is available. Token/trigram and LC overlap is limited to generic shared words ('writes', 'to', 'emergent writing'), which alone does not establish dependency. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence (and the second endpoint's LC evidence) are truncated, so only the bounded excerpts were used.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 1 Reading and Phonics (rank 1), with the first in Term 1 under the 'Emergent reading skills' sub-strand ('Listens to and discusses stories and other texts read aloud') and the second in Term 2 under 'Shared Reading' ('Reads big books or other enlarged texts as a whole class with teacher'), so the permitted developmental direction is Term 1 to Term 2 (first_to_second). The change is substantive rather than mere repeated wording: the Term 1 statement builds oral comprehension and discussion of texts heard read aloud (LCs 'Listens to stories and other texts read aloud' and 'Discusses stories and other texts read aloud'), whereas the Term 2 statement requires the learner to engage with the printed text itself in a whole-class shared reading of big books/enlarged texts. Familiarity with and ability to discuss read-aloud texts plausibly supports success in joint reading of enlarged print with the teacher. Evidence is bounded: source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC metadata are truncated, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, identity scopes and hierarchy.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 Skills (rank 3) about the same punctuation set. The first sits in Grade 3 Term 1, Reading and Phonics > Group Guided Reading, and requires showing an understanding of punctuation (full stops, question marks, exclamation marks, inverted commas) when reading aloud — i.e. receptive recognition of punctuation function in text. The second sits in Grade 3 Term 3, Writing > Shared, Group and Independent Writing, and requires using punctuation correctly in the learner's own writing, with a broadened inventory that adds capital letters and commas. Direction is within one grade from the earlier Term 1 to the later Term 3, which the configured term order permits, and the change is substantive rather than generic repetition: receptive understanding of punctuation marks while reading plausibly supports accurate productive use of the same (and additional) marks in writing. LC evidence agrees (shared 'punctuation' tag; the first LC tags comprehension/reading aloud, the second tags writing/capital letters), confirming the modality shift rather than identical restatement. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so only the bounded excerpts and resolved identity scopes were used; absence of further detail is not proof of absence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1, Term 1 Skills under the same Reading and Phonics Skill Area but different printed sub-strands: 'Shared Reading' (reads enlarged texts such as poems, posters, big books and class stories as a whole class with the teacher) and 'Phonics'/Daily Phonemic Awareness (identifies letter-sound relationships of some single letters, 2 vowels and at least 6 consonants). They are coherent, mutually reinforcing components of early reading instruction taught concurrently in the same term, but the evidence shows parallel daily activities rather than one conferring proficiency needed for the other; teacher-led shared reading does not require independent letter-sound knowledge, and letter-sound identification is not an extension of shared reading. Same-rank (Grade 1, Term 1) direction would need substantive developmental evidence, which the bounded excerpts do not provide; nomination signals (shared ancestors, page proximity, token overlap limited to 'a'/'and') are not semantic grounds for a developmental direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, but the available statement text is sufficient for a symmetric coherence judgment.
